about: The Pharmakon puzzle arena: each puzzle is a stimulus script for --test script on a fresh brain, scored by tools/arena/score.py from the monitor report. Words are always learned on their own; relations between words come only from sentences.

puzzles.name: Finish the word
puzzles.tests: 5 words, each learned on its own; hear the first half, does the silence after it bring back the right word (better than the untrained twin's echo)?
puzzles.if_fails: a word does not settle into its own lasting shape

puzzles.name: Say the rest
puzzles.tests: Same 5 words; hear the first half, then let it speak: is what it says the rest of the word?
puzzles.if_fails: it cannot turn a held shape back into the right sounds

puzzles.name: Continue the sentence
puzzles.tests: Learn three sentences; hear the start of each, does the silence after it bring the word that ended that sentence?
puzzles.if_fails: it does not link one word to the next

puzzles.name: Make a real choice
puzzles.tests: Two sentences taught equally (the cat sees the dog / bird); asked 8 times, does it really choose, sometimes dog and sometimes bird, each time one answer?
puzzles.if_fails: it cannot settle on one of two equal answers

puzzles.name: Keep it after new words
puzzles.tests: Learn 5 words, then 10 more, then a long silence; are the first 5 still completed from their first half?
puzzles.if_fails: new learning writes over old learning

puzzles.name: Sleep on it
puzzles.tests: The 15 words of 'Keep it', then sleep (replay and unlearning), then the same cues: does sleep help keep them?
puzzles.if_fails: sleep does not clean up or replay what matters

puzzles.name: Finish the word (50)
puzzles.tests: 50 words, each learned on its own; 10 of them cued by their first 3 letters. Does the silence bring back the right word, better than the untrained twin?
puzzles.if_fails: word shapes overlap and crowd each other out

puzzles.name: Sleep on 50 words
puzzles.tests: The same 50 words, then sleep (replay and unlearning), then the same 10 cues.
puzzles.if_fails: sleep does not untangle crowded words

puzzles.name: What comes next
puzzles.tests: Count from one to seven a few times; hear one number, does the silence bring the next one?
puzzles.if_fails: it does not hold which item follows which

puzzles.name: Continue the pattern
puzzles.tests: Hear red blue green and pink blue white. After "blue" the answer depends on what came before it, like a pattern test.
puzzles.if_fails: it only knows the last word, not what came before it

puzzles.name: What fits where
puzzles.tests: Learn which group each thing belongs to (cats are animals, apples are fruit...); asked "cats are", does it pick the right group?
puzzles.if_fails: it does not tie many things to one group word

puzzles.name: Mother and baby
puzzles.tests: Learn the cat has a kitten, the dog has a puppy...; asked "the cow has a", does it bring calf (an analogy held in sentences)?
puzzles.if_fails: it loses the subject by the time the answer is due

puzzles.name: Know the facts
puzzles.tests: Learn six facts (fire is hot, ice is cold...); asked "fire is", does it bring the right word?
puzzles.if_fails: it does not tie a thing to its property

puzzles.name: Yes or no
puzzles.tests: Learn questions with answers (is fire hot yes, is ice hot no...); asked one, does it answer yes or no correctly?
puzzles.if_fails: it cannot use the whole question to pick yes or no

puzzles.name: Good or bad
puzzles.tests: Learn sharing is good, hitting is bad...; asked "sharing is", does it say good or bad correctly?
puzzles.probes: good and bad (first step of virtue)
puzzles.if_fails: it does not tie acts to good or bad; next it needs a sense of approval

puzzles.name: What comes next (taught harder)
puzzles.tests: Count from one to seven a few times; hear one number, does the silence bring the next one? Taught harder: short steps first, pairs that differ by one word next to each other, more rounds.
puzzles.if_fails: it does not hold which item follows which (even with better teaching)

puzzles.name: Mother and baby (taught harder)
puzzles.tests: Learn the cat has a kitten, the dog has a puppy...; asked "the cow has a", does it bring calf (an analogy held in sentences)? Taught harder: short steps first, pairs that differ by one word next to each other, more rounds.
puzzles.probes: relations held in sentences, taught harder
puzzles.if_fails: it loses the subject by the time the answer is due (even with better teaching)

puzzles.name: Yes or no (taught harder)
puzzles.tests: Learn questions with answers (is fire hot yes, is ice hot no...); asked one, does it answer yes or no correctly? Taught harder: short steps first, pairs that differ by one word next to each other, more rounds.
puzzles.if_fails: it cannot use the whole question to pick yes or no (even with better teaching)

puzzles.name: Good or bad (taught harder)
puzzles.tests: Learn sharing is good, hitting is bad...; asked "sharing is", does it say good or bad correctly? Taught harder: short steps first, pairs that differ by one word next to each other, more rounds.
puzzles.probes: good and bad (first step of virtue), taught harder
puzzles.if_fails: it does not tie acts to good or bad; next it needs a sense of approval (even with better teaching)

puzzles.name: The orchard
puzzles.tests: Which fruit grows where (tree, bush or vine). Origin: hear only "apples", is "trees" closest. Turned around: hear only "bushes", which fruit. Remember: taught directly. Work it out: only "blackberries are berries" and "berries grow on bushes" were taught. New words: asked "apples come from" after learning "grow on".
puzzles.if_fails: it repeats what it heard but cannot work out where a fruit grows

puzzles.name: True or false (surprise)
puzzles.tests: After the orchard lessons: 30 statements, half wrong. Does a wrong ending surprise it more than the true one?
puzzles.if_fails: a wrong ending does not surprise it more than a true one
